name: Chura Matar
steps: Rinse thick chura briefly in a sieve, drain 10 minutes and fluff. It should soften but retain distinct broad flakes; never leave it immersed in water.
Heat half the ghee in a wide pan, toast cumin, then soften chopped onion, ginger and chilli. Add peas and cook for 5–6 minutes until tender and bright green.
Pour in milk and simmer briefly. Fold in softened chura and salt, then cover over very low heat for 3–4 minutes so the flakes absorb the pea flavors without becoming yellow or mashed.
Switch off heat, add remaining ghee and lemon juice, and toss gently. Let stand covered for 2 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Scatter coriander and serve warm in four bowls. This Banarasi dish should remain pale, moist and strongly studded with peas, unlike turmeric-yellow poha.
tips: Use fresh winter peas when available; this preparation showcases peas rather than spice powder.
passiveTime: Drain rinsed poha for 10 minutes before cooking.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
